scenario: IRET.10.7 / LGRA.10.1.4: if the matched fact has left working memory by the time the body runs, the nested withdraw does nothing, and it is not an error. `k` withdraws the Job before the reply arrives. The reply's body withdraws `j` first and logs "reply" after it, so a runtime that faulted on the dead reference and abandoned the activation would never log "reply". Logs: ["killed 1", "reply"]. PATH PINNED: the reference's lookup missing (`ds_rete_wm_find_by_id` returning NULL in `rete/engine.c`), which takes the no-op branch.
rules_ds:
schema SvcReadReply scope ttl 1_h:
    corr: String
    ok: Bool

service svc.read:
    kwarg n: Int
    response SvcReadReply

schema Job scope explicit:
    id: Int

schema Kill scope explicit:
    id: Int

rule r:
    Job j
->
    call svc.read n: j.id cooldown: 1_min as "c1"
        on response.ok == true:
            withdraw j
            log info "reply"

rule k:
    Kill x
    Job j where j.id == x.id
->
    log info "killed {j.id}"
    withdraw x
    withdraw j
